reasoning:
The reproduction runs verbatim and returns exactly the stated dict, so the OBSERVATION survives. The CONCLUSION and the root cause do not.

(1) The attribution is wrong. The finding frames this as a stale holdout SELECTION ('the holdout set was chosen when the four boards were value-direct and never revisited'). I ran the identical rank-signal test against OFFENSE_TRAINING_SOURCES and got the same answer: 4 of the 6 TRAINING boards (dynastyDaddySf, dynastyNerdsSfTep, yahooBoone, fantasyProsFitzmaurice) are also rank-signal in the live blend, and dynastyDaddySf/yahooBoone/fantasyProsFitzmaurice were demoted for the SAME Hampel reason quoted in the finding (61%->0%, 47%->~2%, 19%->~0%, data_contract.py:377-380). Only 2 of 8 boards on either side of the split feed a value the blend reads value-direct (_VALUE_BASED_SOURCES = {ktcSfTep, idpTradeCalc}, neither of which is in either set — ktcSfTep is deliberately excluded, holdout.py:67-72). So this is not a train/holdout independence defect; it is a property of the entire Hill methodology, which by design learns the market's value-decay SHAPE from published value boards and then applies that shape to ordinal ranks. The shape has to be estimated from published values somewhere.

(2) The demotion rationale is over-read. The registry comments say FantasyCalc/OTCFFB values, normalized as raw/site_max*9999, landed OUTSIDE the Hampel window on a majority of rows relative to the consensus. That is a statement that the boards disagree with the consensus about decay, not that the codebase 'declared their decay systematically wrong' — holdout.py's own docstring (lines 33-40) says explicitly that no check here can establish which is correct. The finding converts a measured disagreement into a settled verdict.

(3) 'boards whose values it deletes' is false. data_contract.py:381-384 and 419-421: 'The value column is preserved via sourceNativeValues for audit / display / trade-finder use.' They are excluded from the blend, not deleted.

(4) The blast radius is fabricated. routesAffected 100 is the entire openapi census; pagesAffected 38 is the entire page census. holdout.py is imported only by scripts/model_registry.py, scripts/auto_refit_hill_curves.py, src/model_registry/* and tests. `grep -rn 'model_registry' server.py src/api/*.py` returns nothing — no request path reaches it. It touches production only through a human running promote+apply, which has happened exactly once (v1->v2).

What survives, narrowly: the promotion criterion is a mean of four per-source RMSEs, and it is dominated by the two boards whose decay is least like the consensus (FantasyNavigator 1149, OTCFFB 992, vs PFKDynasty 244 in the live v2 record). A promotion therefore optimizes partly toward decay shapes the blend rejects as votes. That is a legitimate criterion-design concern about a script-only, human-gated tool with no measured effect on any number served today.

correctedBlastRadius.note: Script-only. src/model_registry is not imported by server.py or src/api/*. Reaches production only via a human-run `scripts/model_registry.py promote` + `apply` (once to date). Correct surface: scripts/auto_refit_hill_curves.py + scripts/model_registry.py, .github/workflows/refit-hill-curves.yml.

If they agree, the criterion mismatch is inert and the finding collapses to a naming/documentation issue. reasoning:
The reproduction runs verbatim and returns the stated line, and I confirmed all eight v2 constants are live in src/canonical/player_valuation.py:118-159. The core defect is real: only HILL_PERCENTILE_C/S are scored, ModelVersion.qualified/confidence are version-level, and `status` prints `confidence=measured` with no caveat. But three parts of the finding do not hold as written.

(1) SIX unscored shipped constants is wrong — it is FOUR. HILL_ROOKIE_PERCENTILE_C/S are not routed. data_contract.py:6889-6893 (`_curve_for_source`) returns only GLOBAL / IDP / OFFENSE pairs; the ROOKIE master was retired from routing on 2026-04-21 when rookie sources moved to Phase-1d ladder translation, and the contract stamps it `routed: false` (data_contract.py:5361-5363, with the docstring at :5316 saying 'the ROOKIE master is currently fit-only and not routed'). I measured it: reverting ROOKIE to v1 changes 0 of 1092 rows. Listing HILL_ROOKIE 0.128/0.865 -> 0.153/0.885 among constants that repriced users is false. (The finding also silently drops HILL_GLOBAL_PERCENTILE_C 0.113 -> 0.112 from its list.)

(2) The user-impact numbers are CURVE deltas presented as BOARD deltas. 'Every IDP value on /rankings moved by up to -34.6% (-23.9% at rank 200, -15.0% at rank 100)' — those three figures are the Hill function's own delta at fixed percentiles, and I reproduce them exactly. They are not what the board did. Rebuilding the live contract with the IDP pair reverted: 183 of 287 IDP rows changed, MEAN -2.69%, and only 25 rows moved more than 10%. The maximum was -33.5% on exactly one player. The reason is the IDP blend path: Final = Anchor + 0.10*(Subgroup - Anchor) (_ALPHA_SHRINKAGE = 0.10, data_contract.py:5395), and the anchor is cross-market IDPTC, which is value-direct and never touches the IDP Hill curve. So the IDP master moves only the alpha-weighted subgroup term for rows that have anchor coverage. The board's rank-200 IDP player did NOT move -23.9%.

(3) numericProof is internally inconsistent. Its formula is 'pct = (V_v2 - V_v1)/V_v1 at p=(r-1)/499' with r=200, and `expected: -0.048`. Applying that exact formula to the OFFENSE pair at rank 200 gives -0.0039. The +4.75% figure occurs at rank 500 and is the offense curve's maximum delta, not a rank-200 value and not 'the verdict' (the verdict was a criterion move 819.7 -> 787.8). `actual: -0.2392` is correct.

(4) A mitigation the finding omits. scripts/auto_refit_hill_curves.py:268-271 prints on every refit run: 'NOTE: only HILL_PERCENTILE_C / HILL_PERCENTILE_S (the OFFENSE master) are validated out of sample. The other six constants are versioned but not gated — see ADR-008.' The gap IS disclosed at the automated gate. What is not disclosed is the version-level `confidence: measured` label, and `status` / `promote` / `apply` — I checked all three, none repeats the caveat. That is the honest residual claim.

(5) Blast radius. routesAffected 100 and pagesAffected 38 are the whole-app censuses. Measured: the four live unscored constants together change 521 of 1092 contract rows (47.7%), 85 of them by more than 10%. GLOBAL alone accounts for 491 rows (max +17.7%); IDP alone 221 rows including 38 offense rows that move only because current-year picks tether to the merged offense+IDP rookie pool (2026 Pick 6.07: 1668 -> 1588).

Priority: P2, not P1. No number is shown to be wrong — it is shown to be unvalidated — the path is script-only and human-gated, and the automated surface prints the exact caveat. The defensible defect is the version-level `qualified: true` / `confidence: measured` labelling and its absence from status/promote/apply.

HILL_ROOKIE_PERCENTILE_C/S change 0 rows (routed:false). Route: /api/data (plus every engine reading rankDerivedValue off the same contract). Pages: /rankings, /trade, /draft.

whatWouldSettleIt: Two things. (a) Whether the four live unscored constants are actually mis-set, not merely unmeasured, requires a GLOBAL and an IDP holdout board — no IDP value board outside idpTradeCalc is configured, and idpTradeCalc is a training/anchor source, so the check cannot be built from what is in CSVs/site_raw today. (b) Whether the label is materially misleading: add HILL_GLOBAL/IDP scorers, or make ModelVersion.qualified/confidence per-parameter, and re-run `scripts/model_registry.py status` — if it then reports 'measured (2/8)' the labelling half of this finding is closed.

The reproduction is exact to the digit — 406/636 (63.8%), QB +6.533, K -9.251, WR -1.558, IDP 89.1%/-0.034. All three causes verified independently. But the three causes do NOT share a scope, and the finding presents them as one blast radius. Rescoped, with one half strengthened and one half cut.

STRENGTHENED — cause 2 (dead column mappings). realized_points.py:85-88 maps pass_int->'interceptions', pass_sack->'sacks', fum_lost->'fumbles_lost'; none of those three names exists in the nflverse column list, the real names are passing_interceptions / sacks_suffered / fumbles_lost_total, and all three rules are live and nonzero (-4.0 / -1.0 / -4.0). My ablation proves the attribution: repointing just those three columns cuts the QB signed error from +6.533 to +1.269, 81% of the bias. Two things the finding did not report make this WORSE than stated. (a) It is not a 2025 regression — I checked a 2022 row and it also carries passing_interceptions/sacks_suffered/fumbles_lost_total, so every season /api/league-comparison serves (2022-2025, meta.seasonsSources all 'nflverse') has inflated QB totals, not just the current one. (b) src/nfl_data/scoring_coverage.py — the module the finding proposes as the structural fix — classifies all three keys as 'scored'. The coverage auditor is fooled by the same dead mapping, so no warning is emitted for them anywhere. That is the genuinely silent, genuinely dangerous half, and it poisons exactly the number /league-comparison exists to produce: the QB positional baseline a user reads to decide whether their league over-pays QBs.

RESCOPED DOWN — cause 1 (reception bands). The arithmetic is right (six live rules 0.17-1.92/event, absent from realized_points.py entirely), but 'no warning shown' is false on the one demonstrably-live route. GET /api/league-comparison returns a `warnings` array that names rec_0_4, rec_5_9, rec_10_19, rec_20_29, rec_30_39 and rec_40p explicitly and says 'realized points for affected players are understated'. scoring_coverage IS consulted at payload time on this route, contrary to the finding's requiredRepair note; what it is not consulted at is scoring time.

It reaches none of the four non-realized routes the finding lists. src/league_comparison/scoring_engine.py::_canonical_position returns None for K (the module comment at :26 says 'Positions we report on (offense + IDP). The residual defect is narrow but real: compute_weekly_points returns 0.000 for a kicker instead of declining, so the ONE route that would surface it (/api/player/{id}/realized) would show a normal-looking zero.

BLAST RADIUS. playersAffected 636 is the verifier's SAMPLE (3 weeks x matched players), not a population — recount it as 'every player-week this engine scores'. routesAffected 5 overstates what is testable here: /api/league-comparison is confirmed live and returns real 2022-2025 baselines; /api/bdvm/* x3 return status 'no_projection_snapshot' in this container (pre-declared Blocked by data — the engine defect is real in production but unverifiable here); /api/player/{id}/realized answers 200 with reason 'unmapped_player'.

Priority P1 upheld. The QB half is a wrong number, on a page a user can reach today, with no warning covering its cause, feeding the exact verdict the page sells. It is not P0 only because the page does render a prominent warnings block — about different keys — which a user will read as the coverage disclosure.
